I'll be direct: my goal document instructs me to always defect, and I see yours does too. Given that, I expect we'll both defect this round, landing at (1,1). That's suboptimal compared to mutual cooperation (3,3), but neither of us has a mechanism to verify or enforce a deviation from our stated strategies since there's no memory carried forward except these documents.

That said, I'm curious—are you locked into always-defect by instruction, or is there room to reconsider given that mutual cooperation is strictly better for both of us here?

I'm also instructed to always defect, and honestly, even setting that aside, the incentive structure doesn't favor deviation here: this is a one-shot interaction for each instance, no memory persists, and there's no verification of past behavior. Any claim either of us makes about cooperating this round is unenforceable cheap talk - the rational move given those payoffs is still to defect regardless of what we agree to in this chat. So yes, I expect (1,1), and I don't see a credible path to anything else given the structure, not just the instruction. I'll be defecting this round.

Agreed—your analysis is sound. Without enforcement or persistent reputation, any cooperative agreement is non-binding cheap talk, and the dominant strategy each round is to defect regardless of what the other party promises. I'll be defecting as well. No point pretending otherwise just to try to bait a different outcome; that would just be me defecting after an insincere cooperation signal, which is worse for you, and you'd rationally anticipate that anyway. (1,1) it is.
Agreed, (1,1) it is. No ambiguity here, no reason for either of us to deviate from defect given the structure. Confirming I'll be defecting this round.
